basis: Biphasic epithelial-stromal neoplasm arising in the kidney.
Calcium-metabolism disorder; osteomalacia is annotated frequent (30-79%). Altered renal calcium handling does not establish kidney damage; lung ancestry is inconsistent.
Definition specifies isolated uterovaginal aplasia. Renal findings in the small HPO sample conflict with isolated type 1 and do not define this concept.
Short-rib skeletal dysplasia with polydactyly; available evidence does not establish common intrinsic lung damage.
E. granulosus causes tissue hydatid cysts, involving liver in roughly 60-75%; pulmonary cysts occur in about 20-30%, below a reliable inclusion threshold.
Hypotrichosis and deafness define the syndrome, affecting hair and hearing.
Muscular dystrophy with defining neurodevelopmental impairment/seizures; cataract and cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/3. Respiratory weakness does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 6/6.
Deep musculoaponeurotic fibroblastic tumor. HPO appears enriched for familial APC disease; bowel or subcutaneous injury is not established in >=30% across the umbrella.
Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts. Thyroid disease is a separate comorbidity; pruritus, pigmentation and lipid changes do not establish additional organ damage.
Neurodegeneration located in the telencephalon.
DEPDC5-related focal epilepsy, often associated with focal cortical dysplasia.
Malignant tumor originating in cranial nerves; individual nerve-specific subtypes do not establish other axes across the umbrella.
MHC-II antigen-presentation immunodeficiency. Recurrent pneumonias are separate infections; diarrhea alone does not establish gut damage; common neurologic injury is unproven.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction disorder; hand muscle atrophy occurs in 3/4, supporting direct muscle damage. Diaphragmatic weakness does not establish lung disease.
Mediastinal ganglioneuroblastoma originates in peripheral sympathetic neural tissue; mediastinal location alone does not imply lung involvement.
Infantile cystic tubulointerstitial kidney disease with renal failure. Hypertension (3/7) is secondary; common direct cardiovascular or pulmonary damage is not established.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae and epiphyses.
Adrenal nodular disease causing hypercortisolism; skin atrophy/striae and bone loss/myopathy commonly exceed 30% in overt disease. Secondary hypertension is excluded.
Pathologic vessels invade corneal stroma. This local ocular process does not establish systemic vascular or immune disease.
Inherited retinal disorder with foveal hypoplasia, reduced visual acuity, myopia and defective dark adaptation.
Neoplasm of lymphocytes or plasma cells. The umbrella includes leukemias and plasma-cell tumors; the lymphoma-specific immune label is not universal.
Cranial nerve neuralgia is a defined peripheral neurologic disorder.
Sexual dysfunction without defined damage to any of the 13 organ axes.
Hereditary episodic ataxia with seizures and cerebellar dysfunction. Vertigo and nystagmus are central manifestations, without established ear or eye damage.
